fields.label: Case number
fields.description: OSHA Form 300 column (A). Year-scoped, because the 300 log is kept per calendar year.

fields.label: What kind
fields.options:
Injury
Illness
Near Miss
Property Damage
fields.description: A Near Miss is not recordable and is the most useful row on this list — it is the one you get for free.

fields.label: Who was hurt
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (B). Left empty for a near miss or property damage.

fields.label: Job title at the time
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (C). A SNAPSHOT, stamped when the case opens and never re-read. A log that quietly re-titles somebody after a promotion is not the record that was made.

fields.label: When it happened
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (D). For an illness, the date of onset.

fields.label: Reported
fields.description: Stamped on insert and never editable. The gap between this and the line above is the thing an inspector looks at.

fields.label: Where it happened
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (E). Plain words — “pump vault, north basin”. A site Link cannot say which part of it.

fields.label: Visit
fields.description: The visit it happened on, when it happened on one.

fields.label: What happened
fields.description: OSHA Form 301 asks these as four separate questions, and it is right to — collapsing them into one box is how a report ends up saying “hurt his back” and nothing an investigation can use.

fields.label: What they were doing just before
What the injury or illness was
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (F), with the body part.

fields.label: What directly harmed them
fields.description: The object or substance — “chlorine solution”, “ladder”, “pump housing”.

fields.label: How it classifies
fields.description: OSHA Form 300 columns (G) to (M). Pick the MOST SERIOUS outcome only — the four are mutually exclusive and ticking two overstates the log.

fields.label: Outcome
fields.options:
Death
Days away from work
Job transfer or restriction
Other recordable case
Not recordable
fields.description: (G) death, (H) days away, (I) transfer or restriction, (J) other recordable.

fields.label: Days away from work
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (K). Calendar days, capped at 180 by the rule.

fields.label: Days on transfer or restriction
fields.description: OSHA 300 column (L). Capped at 180.

fields.label: Injury or illness
fields.options:
Injury
Skin disorder
Respiratory condition
Poisoning
Hearing loss
All other illnesses
fields.description: OSHA 300 columns (M1) to (M6). Exactly one.

fields.label: Treatment
fields.options:
None
First aid only
Medical treatment beyond first aid
Emergency room
Hospitalised overnight
fields.description: First aid ONLY is not recordable; medical treatment beyond it is. That single distinction decides most cases, and it is the one people get wrong.

fields.label: Lost consciousness
fields.description: Recordable on its own, whatever the treatment was.

fields.label: Recordable
fields.description: DERIVED, never typed. See hr_enhancements/safety.py for the rule and for why it is computed rather than judged case by case.

fields.label: Privacy case
fields.description: One of the six categories the rule says must not carry a name on the posted log. Ticking it replaces the name with “Privacy Case” on the 300 log; the name stays on this record and on the separate confidential list.

fields.label: Which category
fields.options:
Intimate body part or reproductive system
Resulting from a sexual assault
Mental illness
HIV, hepatitis or tuberculosis
Needlestick or sharps contaminated with blood
Employee asked for their name to be left off
fields.description: The rule lists six and only six. Recorded because “why is this one anonymous” is the first question anybody asks.

fields.label: Reportable
fields.options:
No
Fatality — 8 hours
Hospitalisation, amputation or eye loss — 24 hours
fields.description: DERIVED. Utah gives 8 hours for a fatality and 24 for an in-patient hospitalisation, an amputation or the loss of an eye. The clock starts when the company learns of it, not when it happened.

fields.label: Call by
fields.description: Computed from `reported_on`. Shown on the form the moment it is filed, which is the only moment it is useful.

fields.label: Equipment must not be touched
fields.description: For a reportable incident the scene stays as it is until UOSH releases it. Ticked automatically when the case is reportable; a human clears it once released.

fields.label: Why it happened
fields.description: Not who. A root cause naming a person is a root cause that changes nothing.
